subject: lk-imp
title: LK.IMP.------ MT.INFO.
description: Diagram in SR(TRS)II-4 (Social Reality / Trans-Information, Level Two) opening Braxton's diagnostic of late-seventies western culture: 'we are creating the future now.' (C)LK-IMP (the concept of linkage implication) is crossed with MT-INFO (multi-information): the question is what linkage-implication produces when crossed with multi-information — the linkage at issue being the connection between American black-culture conditions and world-cultural significance, the multi-information being the spectrum of perceptual claims (the prose lists NBC polls, women's-liberation rhetoric, black-middle-class commentary) that constitute late-seventies western culture's self-image. TH-CONT (theoretical continuance) anchors the upper-right output. SO-EXP-PRI (source-experiential principles) hangs on the right margin. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) sits between subject and partner. (P)DIFF (point-of-activation difference) sits below the central axis. IST-F (interior-source functionalism) anchors the right output. (R)POL-DY (the reality of political dynamics) anchors the lower-center. INFO-DE (information descent) hangs on the lower-right. Structural argument: linkage-implication crossed with multi-information is mediated by affinity-dynamics as central hub. The (p) prefix on DIFF is load-bearing — difference here functions at point-of-activation, not as sustained category. The (r) prefix on POL-DY commits that political-dynamics actually obtains (the prose describes real policies, not hypothetical ones). The diagram exposes Braxton's structural diagnostic: late-seventies western culture treats linkage-implication as if multi-information already settled the case (the NBC poll, the 'enough special treatment' sentiment), but the real structure routes through affinity-dynamics as hub and point-of-activation-difference as the lower mediator — and difference, taken only as point-of-activation, cannot sustain the linkage claim.
